title: Who Am I? Animal Guessing Game for Kids with Milo
description:
Who am I? Play the animal guessing game with Milo the bluebird! Listen to three clues, guess the animal, then see why each fact is true: zebra stripes keep flies away and no two zebras match, pigs roll in mud to keep cool and dig with a strong snout, and a koala is not a bear but carries her joey in a pouch.
An interactive animal guessing game for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: A zebra's stripes make it hard for biting flies to land: horses in striped coats got far fewer fly landings (Caro et al., University of Bristol / UC Davis, PLOS ONE 2019).
Each zebra's stripes are unique, like a human fingerprint; foals can stand and walk soon after birth; zebras eat mostly grass (Live Science, 'Zebra Facts').
Pigs' sweat glands do little to cool them, so they wallow in mud; mud also protects their skin from sunburn (Britannica Kids, 'pig'; Bracke 2011, Applied Animal Behaviour Science).
Pigs root for food with their snouts and have a good sense of smell; piglets are born with a well-developed sense of smell (Britannica Kids, 'pig').
A koala is a marsupial, not a bear; its baby is called a joey and grows in the mother's pouch (San Diego Zoo; Australian Koala Foundation).
Koalas eat mainly eucalyptus (gum) leaves and sleep 18 to 22 hours a day (Australian Koala Foundation, savethekoala.com).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are going to play a guessing game!
Three animal friends are hiding.
I will give you three clues. Then you guess who it is.
Put on your thinking cap. Are you ready? Let's play!

segments.name: zebra
lines: Guess who! Here are three clues.
Clue one. This friend looks like a horse.
Clue two. This friend has black and white stripes.

lines.t: Clue three. This friend lives on the sunny, grassy savanna. Who is it?

lines: It is the zebra! Great guessing!
close:zebra

lines.t: But why does a zebra wear stripes? What do you think?

lines: Here is the fun fact. A zebra's stripes help keep the pesky flies away!
Look. The flies land on the plain brown horse.
exhibit
Let's count the flies on the horse. One, two, three, four, five!
exhibit
But on the stripy zebra? The stripes mix the flies up. They cannot land!
exhibit
And here is one more thing. Every zebra has its own stripes.
close:zebra
No two zebras are the same. The stripes are like your fingerprint!
A baby zebra is called a foal. It can stand up and walk soon after it is born!
What does a zebra eat? Grass, grass, and more grass!
exhibit
Say it with me. Stripes keep the flies away!
close:host
Can you gallop like a zebra? Clip, clop, clip, clop!

lines.t: Quick check! Do the stripes keep the flies away? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! Stripes keep the flies away. You are so clever!

short.title: Why Do Zebras Have Stripes? Guess the Animal!

segments.name: pig
lines: Guess who! Here are three clues.
Clue one. This friend is pink, with a curly tail.
Clue two. This friend lives on the farm.

lines.t: Clue three. This friend says oink, oink! Who is it?

lines: It is the pig! You got it!
close:pig

lines.t: What does a pig do on a hot, sunny day? What do you think?

lines: Here is the fun fact. Pigs roll in the mud to keep cool!
exhibit
When you are hot, you sweat. But a pig cannot sweat much.
So the pig rolls in cool, squishy mud. The mud even stops sunburn, like sunscreen!
exhibit
Now look at that nose! A pig's nose is called a snout.
close:pig
The snout is super strong. A pig uses it to dig in the ground for yummy food.
And the snout can smell very, very well. Sniff, sniff, sniff!
Baby pigs are called piglets. Even a tiny piglet has a super nose!
A pig loves a mud bath, just like you love a cool bath on a hot day!
Say it with me. Pigs roll in mud to keep cool!
close:host
Can you roll your arms like a pig in the mud? Roll, roll, roll!

lines.t: Quick check! Why does a pig roll in the mud? To keep cool? Or to keep warm?

lines: To keep cool! Super thinking!

short.title: Why Do Pigs Roll in Mud? Guess the Animal!

segments.name: koala
lines: Guess who! Here are three clues.
Clue one. This friend is gray and fluffy, with a big black nose.
Clue two. This friend loves to hug a tree.

lines.t: Clue three. This friend munches on green leaves. Who is it?

lines: It is the koala! Well done!
close:koala

lines.t: Now, a tricky question. Is a koala a bear?

lines: No! Here is the fun fact. A koala is not a bear!
Look. This is a bear. A bear has no pouch.
exhibit
But a mama koala has a pouch on her tummy, like a cozy pocket. Her baby rides inside!
teach
A baby koala is called a joey.
close:koala
What does a koala eat? Leaves! Leaves from the gum tree. Munch, munch, munch!
And a koala is a super sleeper. It sleeps almost all day long!
A koala eats leaves, sleeps, eats more leaves, and sleeps again. What a cozy life!
Koalas live far away, in a country called Australia.
Say it with me. A koala is not a bear!
close:host
Can you hug yourself, like a koala hugs a tree? Squeeze!

lines.t: Quick check! What is a baby koala called? A cub? Or a joey?

lines: A joey! You remembered!

short.title: Is a Koala a Bear? Guess the Animal with Milo

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! You guessed all three friends. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Whose stripes keep the flies away?
Who rolls in the mud to keep cool?
Who is not a bear, and rides in a pouch as a baby?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Gallop like a zebra. Roll like a pig. And hug like a koala!
Which friend was the hardest to guess?
Thank you for playing with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
